x: Penny, Cook, Wills, Carter, Bignall and Smith upon winning the Surrey Cross-country Championship. Arthur Penny and Arthur Allum upon being the first men home in the Surrey and Middlesex Cross-country Championships, respectively.

First Jack, then Penny, and afterwards Harold Wills, our second-claim member from Herne Hill Harriers, tried to dispute the lead with Allum, between the bottom of the hill and Beverley Brook, but gave it up in disgust.
After completing a circle round the starting field the leading positions were held by Belton (Surrey A.C.), Cohen (Ashcombe A.C.), Penny, Cook, Stansbury (Ranelagh), and Wills.
